sections.h2: Who handles property tax in Cumberland County, NC?
sections.html:
Real estate here is assessed, and its bills collected, by Cumberland County Tax Administration, which works from the fifth floor of the county courthouse in downtown Fayetteville. Call 910-678-7507; the listed office address is Room 530, 117 Dick Street.

The department's website menu works as a map of what a seller may need: revaluation, real estate appeals, exemptions and exclusions, tax relief programs, payment plans, delinquent taxes, a surplus property list, tax foreclosure sales and a board page. Personal property, business extension, gross receipts and motor vehicle pages sit beside them.

Few North Carolina counties are this large. A July 2025 Census estimate of 338,473 residents compares with 334,728 in the 2020 census, spread across 652.56 square miles of land, about 512.9 people per square mile. Nearly a dozen town and district rates apply inside it, which the table below shows.

sections.h2: What are the Cumberland County property tax rates?
sections.html:
On 2026 bills (fiscal year 2027) the county's general rate is 49.9 cents per $100 of valuation, and a 5.0-cent special recreation rate is listed beside it. Towns levy their own rates as well, so a parcel's total depends on its location.

sections.h2: What flat fees show up on a Cumberland County tax bill?
sections.html:
Several service charges appear on the same bill and sit outside the rate. The county prints these amounts:

  • Solid waste fee of $285 a year for Fayetteville residences with seven or fewer units.
  • Solid waste fee of $130 a year for unincorporated areas and all municipalities except Spring Lake.
  • Refuse tax of $342.72 a year in Hope Mills and $396.00 in Spring Lake, the latter including a $12 residential litter control fee.
  • Fayetteville residential storm water by impervious surface: $84.00 below 2,500 square feet, $168.00 for 2,501 to 4,800, $252.00 beyond that.
  • Residential storm water of $60 a year in Spring Lake and in Hope Mills.
  • Vehicle fees: $25 vehicle fee plus a $5 transit tax in Fayetteville, $10 in Hope Mills, and $5 each in Stedman and Spring Lake.

When you compare a sale offer against your annual carrying cost, look at the bill line by line rather than the rate alone. A move across a town line can change the charges more than the home's value would.

sections.h2: When are Cumberland County taxes due, and what if I am late?
sections.html:
The county's 2026 rate page says bills are due September 1 and need to be paid by January 5 to escape interest, penalties and collection.

After that the statute (G.S. 105-360) charges 2% starting January 6, then three-fourths of one percent for each month or fraction from February 1. MyCCNCPay accepts credit, debit or electronic draft payments, and the same phone number above arranges a payment plan.

The annual listing period for property closes January 31 under G.S. 105-307, and the county posted a reminder of that deadline on January 15, 2026.

Unpaid bills can end in a tax foreclosure sale, which an outside attorney runs for the tax office. The county's foreclosure page names that attorney, and that office has sale dates and parcels in an upset bid period. An owner can still redeem by paying taxes, penalties, interest and costs before the court confirms the sale (G.S. 105-374).

sections.h2: How did the 2025 revaluation work in Cumberland County?
sections.html:
Real property was reappraised countywide for 2025, eight years after the January 1, 2017 revaluation. The county calls this an eight-year cycle, matching G.S. 105-286.

  • February 21, 2025: notices mailed to owners.
  • March 24, 2025: deadline for an informal appeal to Tax Administration.
  • April 23, 2025: Board of Equalization and Review convened.
  • May 28, 2025: deadline for a formal appeal, and the board adjourned.
  • July 1, 2025: new rates using the updated values took effect, with bills mailed that August.

Those dates are history now. The pattern repeats each year in a smaller form: the board convened April 22, 2026, accepted real property appeals until its adjournment on May 20, and set hearings by letter.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Cumberland County assessment?
sections.html:
Start with an informal review, then send a formal request to the Board of Equalization and Review before it adjourns. Delivery options: Room 543 of the courthouse, PO Box 449 in Fayetteville (ZIP 28302), or the secure drop box on the courthouse's rear lot.

Requests must be in writing. An appraiser contacts every taxpayer who appeals, and a letter gives the hearing date and time if the case proceeds to the board. The county suggests appraisals, comparable properties, income and expense statements, repair cost estimates and photos of unusual conditions as evidence.

The regular board's first meeting falls between the first Monday in April and the first Monday in May. Outside a revaluation year it wraps up by the third Monday after starting, unless it needs longer, and cannot sit past July 1. A special board meets at 3:30 p.m. on the second Wednesday of each month except July and approves corrections, clerical errors included. A board decision can be taken to the state Property Tax Commission within 30 days of the notice's mailing (G.S. 105-290).

sections.h2: What do Census figures say about selling a house in Cumberland County?
sections.html:
Owners occupy 55.0% of homes, which leaves about 45% to renters, so rental property is a large part of the market. For 2020-2024 the middle owner-occupied home is valued at $199,200, household income is $61,291 and gross rent is $1,222 a month.

  • Housing units, July 2025: 146,623.
  • Households, 2020-2024: 129,758.
  • Veterans: 40,226.
  • Residents 65 and older: 15.0%.
  • Building permits issued in 2025: 1,547.
  • Mean commute to work: 21.6 minutes.

With 40,226 veterans, the disabled veteran exclusion is worth a check. That program excludes the first $45,000 of appraised value, with no age or income test, using Form NCDVA-9 that a Veterans Service Officer completes first. Elderly or disabled relief and the circuit breaker go through Form AV-9 at the assessor, accepted up to June 1.

faqs.q: When are Cumberland County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Every September 1, with January 5 as the last day before interest. The 2% charge starts January 6.

faqs.q: What is the combined rate inside Fayetteville city limits?
faqs.a: The county lists the City of Fayetteville municipal rate at 0.4495 and the county rate at 0.499, for a combined 0.9485 per $100 on 2026 bills.

faqs.q: Where does a formal appeal go?
faqs.a: Take it to Room 543 of the courthouse, mail it to PO Box 449, or use the secure drop box. It must be in writing and in hand before the board adjourns.

faqs.q: When was the last Cumberland County revaluation?
faqs.a: The 2025 revaluation is the latest, with notices mailed February 21, 2025. The one before it was effective January 1, 2017.

faqs.q: Who runs Cumberland County tax foreclosure sales?
faqs.a: An outside attorney conducts them on behalf of the Tax Office. Call the attorney's office listed on the county's foreclosure page for sale dates and upset bid status.
